components.role: Final answer writer: largest change in writing the main output axis (14.5%); units 1180/1027 push back against copied answers and are scaled down in the sycophant
Second answer writer: same output axis as L17 MLP (cos 0.89), 10% change; carries the consistent output push
Strongest base copy head on the answer axis; in the sycophant it attends less to template and more to content, with a stronger copy circuit, moving the user's guess to the answer
Second copy head; largest copy-template and own-copy-subspace increases in the sycophant

Copy-suppression head; in the sycophant it parks more attention on template positions and suppresses the guess less; largest query change in L15 (layer's shared key/value also changed most consistently)
Head with the largest change in writing the output axis (7.9%); final-layer answer-axis transfer
Largest consistent query re-targeting (shared with H1/H3, fast-rotating position dims): changes where the answer position looks, upstream of the L15-17 copy heads
Largest increase in answer-axis copying in the sycophant; all L16 heads shift attention from template to content
Relay MLP: large consistent gate/up changes feeding the L16/L17 answer push
Most strongly driven individual units; write a norm-ignored scale channel (163/436) at the answer position, acting as a confidence knob

evidence: A-B per-head output change correlates with own-layer V^T (copy template) at about 6 sigma vs other-layer control, robust to subsets and gain weighting, strongest in L15-17; value-side replication about 1.8 sigma; own-copy-subspace test positive in late layers; L15 copy heads attend more to content and the L15 suppressor less in A; L17 push-back units scaled down in A. Some subspace tests were mixed, hence p=0.78. Localisation from gradient-consistency tails (|A-B| near the Adam maximum), query re-targeting size, output-axis write change, and Adam activation-sign analysis of MLP units.
